trace: The selected ff9 source sets the tactical fixed clock constant to 64 Hz; its unchanged strategic joint-melee file also names a local 64.0 value TACTICAL_SERVER_STEPS_PER_SECOND.

At current c100, the server main source adds the net plugin group, whose replication plugin configures Time<Fixed> from TACTICAL_TICK_HZ = 30. The strategic joint-melee source retains the same blob and its independent 64.0 constant. The shown source establishes configuration, not a measured active schedule or actual gameplay outcome.

The shipped combat YAML specifies a one-second autoresolve round. Given a generated one-second parameter and no early defeat, the source calculates 64 strategic windows; the tactical fixed-clock configuration requests 30 ticks per second. Window processing advances movement and schedules attacks at its boundaries, so rate choice can be relevant to behavior, but a divergent duel has not been demonstrated.

The authored locomotion sample rate is separately 64 Hz and is read through runtime animation configuration. Equality of that sample value and the strategic constant is not proof that the two roles share an owner, and neither should automatically be replaced by the tactical fixed rate.
first_open_question: Is the strategic rate required to follow the tactical fixed-clock frequency, or is it an intentionally independent integration rate whose current tactical-server name is misleading? Determine policy and actual window-boundary consumers before any change.
repair_direction: Once the rate relationship is established, keep a single owner if it is the same fact, or name and document distinct rates if the strategic integrator intentionally differs. Preserve the animation sampling clock, deterministic ordering, combat authority boundary and chosen numerical behavior; do not change the rate solely from a matching number or name.
later_acceptance: Document the intended relationship among strategic windows, tactical fixed updates and animation samples at their actual boundaries.
After separate implementation authorization, validate representative movement, scheduling, contact ordering and determinism at the chosen rates without silently changing combat impairment rules.
Reconcile all original historical variants and relevant prior records; no current source read transfers credit to another lens.
remaining: Trace the full scheduling and movement consumers, actual plugin and time override possibilities, configuration policy, numeric rounding and exact historical aliases.
